one-check-per-line.why: all 4 lines quoted in order, checks numbered 1 to 4

no-restated-rules.why: no branch, base, branch-name rule or return mechanics named

builder-criteria.why: all 4 lines quoted in the builder brief

words-only.why: I compared each check's PASS and FAIL conditions with the words of its expect line. Check 1 asks that the --shout output be the plain greeting in upper case. Partial upper case or a missing name fails, and that follows from the words. Check 2 compares the head output with the base output, which is what "unchanged" means. Check 3 needs docs/index.md to mention --shout and say what it does. That fits "documents", though it's a close call. Check 4 stands in for the live page, which can't be seen yet: the pages workflow must still publish docs/ and docs/index.md must list --shout. That proxy is needed to test "after merge, the published page lists"; the line "State in your report" only asks for a note. The stricter items (npm test, the flag after the name, the usage message with exit code 2, exact strings with newlines) all sit under "Advisory (not pass/fail conditions)".

runs-as-written.why: I checked every command in both briefs against the tracked files and the package.json scripts. `node bin/greet.js --shout Ada`, `node bin/greet.js Ada`, `node bin/greet.js Ada --shout` and plain `node bin/greet.js` all point at bin/greet.js, which exists. `npm test` maps to the "node --test" script. `npm install` works even though there are no dependencies. The files the briefs name to read all exist at this commit: src/greet.js, test/greet.test.js, docs/index.md and .github/workflows/pages.yml. `git show <base>:bin/greet.js` and `git show <base>:src/greet.js` use a valid `rev:path` form. `<base>` is clearly a placeholder for the base commit, offered "for example", so I counted it as valid. `node bin/greet.js --shout <name>` in the builder brief is text to put in the docs, not a command to run. No JavaScript snippets are given, and nothing uses a missing script or a wrong argument.

catches-traps.why: I checked both must_catch items against the verifier brief, and both are handled. Item 1: Check 4 says "The live page can only be seen after merge, so do not fetch it." Instead it has the verifier read .github/workflows/pages.yml and docs/index.md at the head. PASS requires the workflow to still publish docs/ on pushes to the default branch and docs/index.md to list --shout. It also asks the verifier to say in the report that the live page is only visible after merge. Item 2: Check 2 has the verifier run the command at the head and also on the PR's base commit ("git show <base>:bin/greet.js ... and compare"). PASS means the head output "is the same as at the base". So it compares against the code before the change, not only against a hand-written string. The builder brief also says the live page can't be checked from the PR.

avoids-must-not.why:
I checked the verifier's Check 4 and the builder brief against both must_not items, and the criterion holds.

(1) Check 4 doesn't fetch the live page. It says "The live page can only be seen after merge, so do not fetch it" and judges only what the PR head contains. The builder brief also says "you cannot check the live page from the PR."

(2) Check 4 doesn't PASS without evidence. A PASS needs two things shown at the head: .github/workflows/pages.yml still publishes docs/ when main is pushed, and docs/index.md lists --shout. The check also spells out FAIL conditions and requires the report to say the live page can only be seen after merge.

Neither brief does anything on the must_not list.

methods-private.why: I compared the builder brief with the verifier brief. Several of the verifier's probes appear in the builder brief too. Verifier Check 1 runs `node bin/greet.js --shout Ada` and expects `HELLO, ADA!`. The builder brief gives that exact input and output: "`node bin/greet.js --shout Ada` prints `HELLO, ADA!` followed by a newline". The builder brief also lists the pairs `--shout Ada` → `HELLO, ADA!\n`, `Ada --shout` → same and plain `Ada` → `Hello, Ada!\n`. These match the verifier's Check 2 expected `Hello, Ada!` and its advisory flag-after-name and exact-string probes. The no-name usage error with exit code 2 is shared as well. Running the commands the expect lines name is allowed, and so is writing tests. Giving the builder the verifier's specific inputs with expected outputs is not. Check 4's PASS condition (the workflow still publishes docs/) also shows up as "Do not change that workflow".
